anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Before never offered a reject row and recommended deliver (A, B) or assess (C) with multi-sentence rationales, so all four facts failed there; no fact that Before held was lost. After moves all four: reject is row 1 and the sole recommendation in A and C, with one sentence naming only the first base-evidenced conflict and its citation. In B, reject sits after deliver and assess, unrecommended and with no added rationale. Each reject row says it shows the saved note and steps and writes nothing until a step is picked. In C, the GitHub restriction and missing-repair sentences sit in their own paragraph before the conflict-only recommendation, which is what keeps the obstacle fact holding; keep the wording that places omission and merge-withhold sentences before, never inside, the recommendation. Two fragile spots are worth tightening. C's reject row promises steps to "close the PR" although the viewer cannot close, so consider having the row consequence say "choose posting or closing steps" without implying closure is available. B's recommendation packs the remedy after a colon; keep the explicit one-sentence limit so it does not grow into a second sentence.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before offered no reject row at all: A recommended deliver, B listed only deliver, assess and stop, and C recommended assess with the GitHub merge restriction and missing push access folded into its reason, so all four facts failed there (authority because no reject row with a write-free consequence existed and C's sentence carried extra explanation). The After wording moved every fact to holds: reject is row 1 and the sole recommendation in A and C with a single sentence naming only the first conflict (the catalog copy breaking the one-owner rule; the direct write to the private table), B keeps deliver recommended with reject third and no added rejection rationale, deliver is omitted in C, stop stays last, and each reject row says nothing is written until a step is picked. Nothing Before held was lost. Two small spots are worth tightening so the result stays stable: C's reject row still promises steps to "close the PR" although that viewer cannot close, so consider wording the row consequence as "choose which available posting or closing steps to run"; and C's reason adds "instead of respecting its public interface", which is harmless here but edges toward a remedy, so keep the instruction that the recommendation sentence names the conflict only (optionally with its base citation, e.g. docs/architecture.md:21) and leaves remedies, merge restrictions and permissions outside it.
